status.tripped: {mode} stopped: the strip is not responding
status.trippedManual: {mode} stopped: the strip is not responding, auto-retry gave up. Turn the strip on or pick a mode to resume
field.version.label: HueLink version
field.version.description: The extension version that is actually loaded. The source is the VERSION constant in huelink.mjs.
field.status.label: HueLink status
field.status.description: One line about what the strip is doing right now. The circuit breaker shows up here too ('... stopped: the strip is not responding'), which is the only way to tell a deliberately dark strip from a strip that has stopped answering.
field.fpsReal.label: HueLink real frames
field.fpsReal.description: How many frames really went out in the last 5 s window. 'Frame cap' is the target, this is the delivery.
field.dropped.label: HueLink dropped frames
field.dropped.description: Frames that were deliberately not sent (too little change + the per-window quota), since startup. Without this number a low 'real frames' reading looks exactly the same whether suppression is working or the strip is not responding.
field.mode.label: HueLink mode
field.mode.description: Light / Effect / Sync. The same thing the Home Assistant mode picker does; choosing a mode while the strip is off also turns it on.
field.preset.label: HueLink picture preset
field.preset.description: Sets the frame cap, air budget, fade length, scene cut settings and saturation at once. Normal is the shipped defaults, so it is the way back. Sports, Games and Music take more of the Zigbee coordinator than Normal; Movies takes less. Moving any slider afterwards is allowed and clears the selection.
field.fps.label: HueLink frame cap
field.fps.description: Target frame rate for sync and effects. The floor is 2 so there is still a way to deliberately hand the air back to the rest of the house; the ceiling is {max}, because above that the occupancy budget trims the frames anyway.
field.delta.label: HueLink delta threshold
field.delta.description: How large a colour change has to be before a frame is worth sending, as % of the measured default. Higher = quieter air and more visible steps in slow fades, lower = smoother and more expensive.
field.duty.label: HueLink frame quota
field.duty.description: How many frames may go out in a single 100 ms window. This is the burst cap: it stops a sudden scene change from firing off a whole series at once and locking the coordinator away from the rest of the house.
field.budget.label: HueLink air budget
field.budget.description: Share of the Zigbee coordinator's time the strip may take, in %. This is the knob that really decides the frame rate: one frame costs about 51 ms, so 35% buys roughly 7 frames a second, and raising the frame cap above that changes nothing until this goes up too. Turn it up and the strip follows the picture more closely, while every other Zigbee command in the house waits a little longer for its turn.
field.smoothing.label: HueLink fade length
field.smoothing.description: How long the strip takes to fade between two ordinary frames, as a multiple of the gap between them. Kept just above 1 so the colour never comes to rest between frames, which is the stutter this exists to remove. Higher looks creamier and sits further behind the picture, lower looks sharper and starts to flicker.
field.cutThreshold.label: HueLink scene cut threshold
field.cutThreshold.description: How big a colour jump has to be before it counts as a scene cut and gets the fast fade instead of the slow one. Low means nearly every change is treated as a cut, so the strip feels snappy but the frame cap stops controlling the rate; high means only a real cut to black or to a new scene qualifies, and 40 switches the fast path off.
field.cutMs.label: HueLink scene cut fade
field.cutMs.description: How fast the strip lands on the new colour when a scene cuts, in ms. The first of the two strobe knobs: at 50 ms a quick flash arrives smeared, at 0 to 20 ms it lands as a flash. Very short values read as a click rather than a fade on some strips, which is why the default is not 0.
field.cutPerSec.label: HueLink scene cuts per second
field.cutPerSec.description: How many times a second a scene cut may jump the queue and go out ahead of the frame clock. The second strobe knob, and a ration rather than a switch: at 1 almost every flash of a fast strobe is swallowed, at 3 to 5 the strip visibly flashes along with it. Each one is an extra frame of coordinator time, so the worst case is the frame cap plus this.
field.saturation.label: HueLink saturation
field.saturation.description: How vivid the colours are, in %. 100 means the pixels go out exactly as the TV sent them, which is what every earlier version did. Above 100 pulls each colour away from grey, so a washed-out picture gets its punch back; past about 170 the mid-tones start collapsing onto flat primaries and the gradient loses detail. Below 100 is the opposite and useful for a strip that is too loud at night. This is the one setting here that costs the Zigbee coordinator nothing: it changes the colours inside a frame, not how many frames there are.
log.configDefaults: no settings file, running on the built-in defaults
log.configSame: config changed, but no pacer value is different
log.configRestartNeeded: config changed: {fields} only take effect after a zigbee2mqtt restart
log.fpsCapped: frame cap asked for {asked} fps, {effective} is what can be paid for: the frame quota allows {duty} and the air budget allows {budget} at {sendMs} ms a frame. Raise 'HueLink frame quota' and 'HueLink air budget' to actually get {asked}.
log.fpsUncapped: frame cap {asked} fps is now deliverable: quota allows {duty}, budget allows {budget}
log.deviceNotFound: device '{device}' not found, the extension will not run
log.startReset: startup reset sent, the strip is back under normal z2m control
log.wasLit: the strip was lit after the restart: turning it off, the mode is chosen by a person or by the TV
log.udpBoundOpen: UDP {bind}:{port} accepts frames from any sender; set 'udpAllowFrom' to limit that
log.udpRejected: {packets} UDP frames dropped in {window} s: sender not in 'udpAllowFrom' ({senders})
log.resumed: {mode} resumes: the source is sending again
log.sourceEnded: {mode} ended: the source went quiet ({ttl} ms without a frame), strip turned off
log.sourceEndedArmed: {mode} ended: the source went quiet ({ttl} ms without a frame), strip turned off, waiting for frames to come back
log.sourceQuiet: {mode} selected, but the source is quiet: strip turned off
log.sourceQuietArmed: {mode} selected, but the source is quiet: strip turned off, waiting for frames
log.blackGated: the sync source has been black for {seconds} s: treating it as no signal, the strip goes off until a lit frame arrives
log.blackEnded: the sync source has light in it again: sync resumes
log.tripped: {mode} stopped, strip turned off: the strip is not responding ({limit} frames in a row, last error: {error})
log.autoRetryGaveUp: {mode} stopped {streak} times in a row without a recovery: auto-retry is giving up, a manual resume is needed
log.effectModeEmpty: effect mode with no effects loaded, ignored
log.badValue: '{field}' = {value} is not a usable value, ignored
log.commandNotObject: command payload is not an object, ignored: {payload}
log.entityStateFailed: handling a strip state publish failed: {error}
log.effectMissingFields: effect without 'kind' or an 'effect.<id>' name in i18n, skipped: {entry}
log.effectDuplicate: effect name '{name}' is not unique, skipped
log.effectUnknownKind: effect '{name}' asks for an unknown generator '{kind}', skipped
log.effectSelectFailed: effect '{effect}' could not be started, nothing selected
log.presetBadId: preset without a usable 'id' and 'name', skipped: {entry}
log.presetDuplicate: preset '{id}' has an already used id or name, skipped
log.presetBadKnob: preset '{id}' has no usable '{knob}', skipped: a preset must set every knob, or choosing it would leave the strip half changed
log.presetFpsTrimmed: preset '{name}' asks for {asked} fps, this installation allows {max}. Raise 'maxFps' in huelink.config.json only if the coordinator can carry it (see README, 'Separate coordinator')
log.frameFailed: frame send failed ({n}/{limit}), pausing {pauseMs} ms before the next try: {error}
log.stalled: the picture reached the strip {total} ms late: {causes}
log.stallCause.backoff: pause after a failed frame {ms} ms
log.stallCause.window: frame quota per 100 ms used up {ms} ms
log.stallMore: (+{count} more like this in the last seconds, not logged)
